cohort: The study included 300 women, equally split between those who had vaginal births and those who had cesarean sections.
finding: Cesarean delivery, increased need for postpartum support, and postpartum depression were significant predictors of lower breastfeeding success in the first postpartum month.
mod_finding: Cesarean delivery was identified as a significant predictor of lower breastfeeding success, with mothers who had a cesarean section, received inadequate postpartum support, and were at risk of postpartum depression showing the lowest success rates.
cross-section timing: Measurements were taken during the first postpartum month.
